title: What Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 Is
definition: Programmable Matter Systems 2.0: next-gen matter that reshapes on command.
description:
Programmable Matter Systems 2.0: next-gen matter that reshapes on command. This is Future Materials at its most ambitious — catom arrays research, matter logistics engineering and shape programs operations converging on a single goal: making matter hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Materials will decide power delivery outcomes this century. Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working matter hulls, the larger catom arrays vision stalls, and with it, the matter logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Programmable Matter Systems 2.0
definition: Today's documented research behind Programmable Matter Systems 2.0.
description:
The road to Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 is already being paved. The Materials Genome Initiative accelerates computational discovery of new materials. Metamaterial cloaking research (Duke, Imperial College) bends light, sound and heat around objects.

MIT's programmable-matter and self-assembly labs prototype shape-shifting materials. Together these programs form the catom arrays foundation that Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 will build on — the matter logistics results, the shape programs methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as matter logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

definition: Estimates Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a matter hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 6063 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where catom arrays monitoring, matter logistics redundancy, or shape programs maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Programmable Matter Systems 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Programmable Matter Systems 2.0 — next-gen matter that reshapes on command.

Phase 1 — Prove (catom arrays): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (matter logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (shape programs): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (power delivery): matter hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and manufacturing-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
